behaviour: arguments out, dex, mode byte, payload byte, optional address set, byte. Users are dex +0xf8 (user_to_state). Set given: that set. Otherwise byte != 0 or dex +0x1a0 != 0: the whole table. Otherwise the set at dex +0x158 (users_with_positions). A given set wins, even an empty one

the set becomes a vector of pointers to its keys, the fold runs, the rows of every list node are inserted one at a time into a B-tree set. The same two functions are what the ADL core 0x36f7c40 calls directly

users empty: every address skipped with no hash. Else hash, probe; an address not in the table is skipped; found: 0x37d7360(row, address, mode, payload, dex +0x60, dex) gives a vector of 0x30 rows, joined to the fold's vector

bucket order pairs (address, row), the same builder per pair, the (address, rows) items in a B-tree map by address, then all rows flattened, sorted, equal rows dropped and bulk built. 0 rows gives root 0
address bytes, tag, word 1 only with both tags not 0, word 2 signed. Word 1 of a cross row is never read, and the builder leaves it unset
a list of pointers to (id, side) keys, the users object, the oracle table and the dex. One 0x28 row per key is collected first, and only then inserted into the out map, in list order
side byte 2 in a result row ends the fold, and 0x3889650 then panics on the short count. Side is a bool niche, so 2 cannot come from a real key
byte +0xa8 of the users object (dex +0x1a0) != 0: every pair of the table. Otherwise the keys of the set at +0x60 (dex +0x158). A key always gets a row, empty set included

users empty: nothing. Else 0x36f5d40(id, side, oracle, dex, address, row); a result with word 0 != 1 drops the user, a kept one is (score, address), 0x20 bytes. The pair fold also keeps the address as a 0x38 row
rows go one at a time into a set ordered by (score word, address)
rows first go to a map by address, then into a vector of its values, sorted by the same order and bulk built
score bits x: sign clear gives x | 2^63, sign set gives !x, compared unsigned, then address bytes. This is f64 total order: NaN at the two ends, -0 below +0
out map keyed (id, side). The same key again replaces the set and the old one is dropped. A key with no candidate stays in the map with root 0, and the ADL core panics on it only when size is left
